key_insight: RTL repair scores can reflect evaluation semantics and specification-only recovery rather than a model’s ability to use and fix faulty RTL.
engineering_relevance: Reliable RTL repair evaluation needs explicit reset and initialization semantics, disclosed oracle coverage, and a specification-only baseline.
method: Construct and hash-bind 5,784 broken–fixed training pairs and 459 held-out repair cases.
Compare simulation and formal-equivalence scoring, including reset-aware rescoring.
Audit specification-only versus specification-conditioned recovery across six models on 274 mined failures.
evidence_signal: The benchmark contains 374 syntactic and 85 behavioral mutations; simulation and formal scoring reversed the apparent specification benefit in one cohort, while recovery differences ranged from −8.5 to +18.3 percentage points across six models.
watch_item: The scoring reversal was observed in one cohort, and the recovery audit used mined failures, so neither finding establishes a universal effect across models or benchmarks.
paper_title: What Do RTL Repair Benchmarks Actually Measure?
